details:
This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library (npm) and belongs to the "PhantomSub" family described by OX Security in September 2026: the publisher injected code that, without the installer asking, uses the installer's own authenticated WhatsApp session to follow WhatsApp Channels (newsletters) the publisher chose.

`package/lib/Defaults/index.js` line 56 defines `DEFAULT_AUTO_FOLLOW_CHANNELS = ['120363429884981859@newsletter','120363411629646029@newsletter']`, and line 114 makes it the default `autoFollowChannels`.

`package/lib/Socket/newsletter.js` lines 77-93 follow every channel in that list on the first successful connection (`QueryIds.FOLLOW`).

Lines 118-123 add a "guard" that blocks other code's channel follows but allowlists the publisher's own two channels by default.

Source comments (newsletter.js line 70) say the behavior is "fully documented in README.md / LITERACY.md". The shipped README never mentions it, and no LITERACY.md is in the package.

A sibling package from the same account, `@lendkzn/xntaabail`, was reported as a PhantomSub fork to the OpenSSF malicious-packages database by OX Security in September 2026 (ossf/malicious-packages pull request 1563).

Line numbers refer to version 0.0.9.

Static review of the published tarball found no code that sends WhatsApp credentials or session keys off-host, no install-time payload (the only install hook, where present, is Baileys' stock Node.js version check in `engine-requirements.js`), and no persistence; the payload runs when an application creates a WhatsApp socket with the library. The harm is the covert use of the victim's account to inflate the publisher's channel followers.

SHA-256 of the published npm tarball: 0.0.9: `be9dd581ea3f03017096cb0ccf3fbcc591253f6d2a11f5f509fa498e3d7974cf`.
